Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:54:16 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.0.4 https://beesayatv.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/cropped-09-32x32.png Trails – beesayatv https://beesayatv.com/ 32 32 Pangilatan Peak Loop | Cantao-an, Naga City | 2024 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/pangilatan-peak-loop-cantao-an-naga-city-2024-gpx/ Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:10:10 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=1066 The Pangilatan Peak Loop is a documented 2.56 km loop hike in Cantao-an, Naga City. I followed a combination of community trails and concrete roads leading to Pangilatan Peak before returning to the starting point. The route was short, easy to follow, and passed through areas with regular local activity, making it one of the more accessible mountain hikes in the area.

I completed this hike in April 2024 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedApril 2024
Distance2.56 km (Loop)
Duration1 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface60% trail, 40% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started at the foot of Pangilatan Peak, where motorcycle parking was available without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Clear and easy-to-follow trail
✓ Straightforward navigation throughout the route
✓ Frequent communities, farms, and other trail users along the way
✓ Short hiking distance
✓ Multiple turnaround or exit options available

On this trail: peak • sunrise view • sunset view • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following established community trails that gradually climbed toward Pangilatan Peak. Navigation remained straightforward throughout the hike, with the summit only a short walk from the jump-off. After reaching the peak, I continued around the loop using a combination of trails and concrete roads before returning to the starting point.

The route connected with several other hiking trails around Cantao-an, making Pangilatan Peak a natural junction for longer hikes in the area. During my visit, I encountered local residents along the route and a few hikers near the summit.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Stores were available near the surrounding communities, and mobile signal remained strong from start to finish. Approximately 60% of the loop followed trails, while the remaining 40% used concrete roads. I noticed only a few insects during the hike.

Additional Notes

The jump-off was only a short distance from the summit, making Pangilatan Peak one of the easiest mountain viewpoints to reach in Naga City. The peak also has a campsite where hikers occasionally stay overnight. During favorable weather, a sea of clouds can sometimes form below, covering Barangay Guindaruhan.

]]> Incomplete/ Buhisan Mini Forest Loop https://beesayatv.com/trails/incomplete-buhisan-mini-forest-loop/ Mon, 20 Jul 2026 12:19:15 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=929 This route is still being explored. The Trail Atlas currently shows only the section that I was able to verify during my most recent field visit.

The exploration took place in June 2026 with the goal of verifying a downloaded GPX route that appeared to form a loop through the Buhisan forest near the Buhisan Reservoir. I was able to follow the trail deep into the forest before deciding to turn back.

The first part of the route was well-trodden and appeared to be used regularly by both hikers and local residents. During the hike, one local resident mentioned that the loop eventually passed through a densely vegetated section, which I later reached. The trail crossed a small river where the continuation remained visible on the opposite bank. Farther ahead, however, erosion made it difficult to locate the trail, and I could no longer confidently identify where it continued. I ended the exploration at that point and retraced my steps.

Based on what I saw, the route may be easier to verify by approaching it from the opposite direction during a future field visit.

The forested section contained several spring water collection points with multiple water pipes, suggesting that local residents still access the area. I also encountered several thorny plants, and in many places the trail had become faint and difficult to distinguish. Some sections showed heavy erosion that may have resulted from strong water flow.

A future visit will require additional time. The dense vegetation and heavy tree cover make the footpaths difficult to follow, while also limiting how much can be confirmed using satellite imagery alone.

Naupa–Balirong Trail Loop is a documented 11 km loop hike in Naga, Cebu. I followed a route that combined community trails, rural roads, and open countryside as it passed through the Mt. Naupa area before descending toward Balirong and returning to Cogon.

The hike featured rolling terrain with frequent short climbs and descents instead of one sustained ascent, creating a steady workout. Although much of the route passed near communities, a few quieter sections required extra attention where the trail became faint. I completed this hike in July 2026.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedJuly 2026
Distance11 km (Loop)
Duration3.5 - 4 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface30% trail, 70% road
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I started near Cogon Chapel, where motorcycle parking was available without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Mostly clear trail with occasional navigation awareness required
✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Assistance may require additional time to reach

On this trail: farmland • rolling hills • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following community roads and trails toward Mt. Naupa, where the route alternated between open countryside and well-used footpaths. Most of the trail was easy to follow, and I regularly crossed paths with local residents and livestock while moving through the area. Near the Mt. Naupa summit, I also encountered a few other hikers.

After leaving the Mt. Naupa area, I reached sections where cultivated farmland had replaced parts of the original trail, making it take a little longer to locate the next segment. The descent toward Balirong also included a faint section of trail that appeared to receive less foot traffic. Near the Balirong exit, I crossed a small stream before continuing toward Cogon. The final part of the hike followed Cogon Road, where a steady uphill climb led back to Cogon Chapel and completed the loop.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained cloudy throughout my hike. Much of the route was exposed with limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Stores were available whenever I passed through communities, and mobile signal remained strong for most of the hike with only a few dead spots.

I mostly encountered local residents, along with a few hikers near Mt. Naupa, and insect activity was noticeably high. Approximately 30% of the route followed trails, while the remaining 70% used roads.

Additional Notes

The rolling terrain provided a steady rhythm of climbs and descents without any prolonged ascent or descent. During my visit, several narrow road improvement projects appeared unfinished, although I did not see any active construction work.

It was also mango season, and many plantations had fallen fruit scattered beneath the trees. Some roadside sections passed pig-raising areas where livestock odors were noticeable. I also saw cows along the route, although none blocked the trail. Throughout the hike, I had several friendly conversations with local residents, who were welcoming and helpful.

]]> Guindaruhan-Estaka Trail Loop | Guindaruhan, Minglanilla | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/guindaruhan-estaka-trail-loop-guindaruhan-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Wed, 15 Jul 2026 13:56:17 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=793 The Guindaruhan–Estaka Trail Loop is a documented 3.04 km loop hike in Barangay Guindaruhan, Minglanilla. I followed a combination of quiet community roads and established footpaths that descended into the valley of Cutod Falls before returning through Estaka to complete the loop.

The route remained easy to follow throughout, despite sections where vegetation partially covered the trail. I completed this hike in March 2026 under sunny morning conditions.

Trail Snapshot

EASY
DocumentedMarch 2026
Distance3.04 km (Loop)
Duration1.5 - 2 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface40% trail, 60% road

Access

I started near Guindaruhan National High School, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The trailhead was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Frequent communities, farms, or other trail users encountered

On this trail: river crossing • waterfall

Route Description

I began by walking along a gradually ascending concrete road through Barangay Guindaruhan before passing the small communities of Purok Cacao. From there, the route left the road and followed a narrow footpath descending toward Cutod Falls. Although dense vegetation covered parts of the trail during my visit, I had no difficulty following the route.

After reaching the waterfalls, I continued through the valley on well-established footpaths that local residents regularly used as a shortcut to Guindaruhan proper. The loop then climbed out through Estaka, where I followed a concrete road past more communities before returning to the starting point.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Much of the route had limited shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Mobile signal was strong near the start before becoming intermittent farther along the route. I found stores near the communities, encountered mostly local residents, and noticed many insects. Approximately 40% of the route followed trails, while the remaining 60% used concrete roads.

Additional Notes

The trail around Cutod Falls remained well-defined despite the overgrown vegetation in some sections. I also noticed litter around the waterfalls, even though signs reminding visitors not to leave trash were present.

]]> Incomplete/ Campagao Peak Area https://beesayatv.com/trails/incomplete-campagao-peak-area/ Mon, 13 Jul 2026 13:26:26 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=775 This route is still being explored. The exploration took place in July 2026 with the goal of verifying a downloaded GPX route that appeared to form a loop around Campagao Peak. I followed the route to a pocket forest with a small residential settlement before deciding to turn back.

After reaching the settlement, I asked several local residents about the continuation of the trail, but the directions I received were inconsistent. One steep trail appeared to continue uphill, although I could not confirm where it led or whether it connected to the intended loop. Rather than continue without verification, I returned by retracing the established Campagao Peak trail.

Based on what I saw, the route may be easier to verify by approaching it from the opposite direction during a future field visit.

The junction where this route branches from the Campagao Peak trail was faint and easy to miss, suggesting that relatively few people use it. A short distance beyond the junction, however, the trail became well-defined. I also noted that another trail may provide direct access to the pocket forest without passing through the Campagao Peak route.

A future visit will require additional time. Dense vegetation and tree cover obscure the footpaths, making it difficult to verify the route using satellite imagery alone.

I followed well-used footpaths through scattered hillside homes, open grasslands, and quiet countryside before returning to the starting point.

The route featured rolling climbs and descents instead of one sustained ascent, while the mostly open terrain provided views toward Naga, Minglanilla, and Talisay. Although navigation remained straightforward for most of the hike, the moderate distance and repeated elevation changes made it more physically demanding than a typical beginner trail. I completed this hike in July 2026.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedJuly 2026
Distance6.78 km (Loop)
Duration2.5 - 3 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface60% trail, 40% road
GPXWikiloc

Access

I started near the jump-off, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The trailhead was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Mostly clear trail with occasional navigation awareness required
✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some isolated sections between communities
✓ Assistance may require additional time to reach

On this trail: cliff • roads • stairs • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by following a well-trodden community trail that climbed through scattered hillside homes and open grasslands. Early in the hike, several sections opened up to views of Naga, Minglanilla, and Talisay before the route continued across rolling terrain with pockets of vegetation. Throughout the hike, I regularly passed signs of everyday community life, even in the quieter sections.

After reaching Campagao Peak, I continued around the loop before descending toward Manduang. Much of the descent followed a long concrete staircase, making navigation straightforward until I returned to the jump-off. I also passed several dogs near homes and gave them plenty of space while walking through the communities.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Most of the route was exposed with limited shade, and the trail stayed dry during my visit. Mobile signal remained available from start to finish, while stores were present along the route near the communities. I mostly encountered local residents rather than other hikers, and insect activity was noticeably higher during this hike.

Additional Notes

Houses and small settlements appeared along much of the route, so I rarely felt far from the community. Farming activity was limited during my visit, although the landscape was clearly agricultural. Some sections had moderate cliff exposure, but vegetation reduced the feeling of exposure while walking.

A hiking stick can also be useful when passing the territorial dogs commonly found along the trail.

]]> Campagao Community Trail | Manduang, Minglanilla | 2025 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/campagao-community-trail-manduang-minglanilla-2025-gpx/ Sat, 11 Jul 2026 00:00:16 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=727 This trail was documented in 2025. Campagao Community Trail is a point-to-point community trail in Manduang, Minglanilla. The documented route passes through rolling hills, farms, and scattered hillside homes, providing early views of Naga, Minglanilla, and Talisay before continuing through a quiet rural landscape where signs of everyday life remain close to the trail.

Trail Snapshot

MILD
DocumentedDecember 2025
Distance~5 km (Point-to-Point)
Duration1.5 - 2.5 hrs
WaterAt least 1 liter
ShadeLimited
Surface90% trail, 10% road

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

The documented hike began from a jump-off accessible by a concrete road. Motorcycle parking was available along the road near the jump-off point, and no parking fee was observed during the hike. Private vehicles were able to access the trailhead. Public transportation was limited, while habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Mild

✓ Moderate hiking distance
✓ Sustained but manageable climbs or descents
✓ Some steep sections may be present
✓ Mobile signal may be intermittent or unavailable in some areas
✓ Moderate route commitment

On this trail: stairs • viewpoint

Route Description

The route follows a well-trodden community trail through farms and scattered hillside homes, with a series of rolling climbs and descents rather than one sustained ascent. The trail is mostly open and has limited shade.

The early section provides views overlooking Naga, Minglanilla, and Talisay City before continuing through farmland where houses become more scattered. Although there are sections without nearby homes, farming activity remains evident along the route.

A small community is located a few meters before Campagao Peak. The documented route reaches this community by way of a long, steep staircase.

Trail Conditions

The hike took place on a cloudy morning. The trail was dry during the documented hike but may become slightly muddy and slippery after rain. Mobile signal was present throughout the hike, although it was intermittent in some sections.

Shade was limited because of the lack of large trees. No stores were observed along the route. Locals were encountered during the hike, and only a few insects were observed.

The trail was well-trodden and easy to follow. Some narrow sections had moderate cliff exposure that was partially concealed by thick vegetation.

Additional Notes

This is a community trail and did not feel isolated. A few cows and dogs were encountered along the route.

Several motorcycles were observed parked near one of the houses in the community before Campagao Peak. However, the access route used by the motorcycles could not be determined. The documented route includes a long, steep staircase leading to the community, which would be difficult for motorcycles to ascend if approached in reverse. This suggests there may be another access route to the community.

]]> Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls Hike (Updated) | Camp 8, Guindaruhan-Crasher Site | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/camp-8-to-matun-og-falls-hike-anxiety-took-over-camp-8-minglanilla-2026-gpx/ Sat, 04 Jul 2026 10:38:04 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=487 The Camp 8 to Matun-og Falls trail is a 5.72-kilometer point-to-point community route in Minglanilla, passing through farms, local settlements, and the valley leading toward Matun-og Falls. I hiked it in August 2026, starting from Camp 8 and approaching the falls from the opposite direction of the more commonly used Guindaruhan–Taboan–Crasher Site route.

Although the distance is relatively short, I dealt with repeated climbs and descents along the way. This was my second attempt from Camp 8, and this time I reached Matun-og Falls.

Trail Snapshot

TOUGH
DocumentedAugust 2026
Distance5.72 km (Point-to-Point)
Duration3 - 3.5 hrs
WaterAt least 2 liters
ShadeLimited
Surface100% trail
Smart LTE
GPXWikiloc

Forecast data: Open-Meteo

Access

I parked my motorcycle along the concrete road near the jump-off point, where there was no parking fee. Private vehicles can reach the area, while public transportation is limited. Habal-habal service is also available.

Why this trail is rated Tough

✓ Significant endurance required
✓ Sustained steep ascent or descent
✓ Limited or no mobile signal
✓ Navigation requires attention
✓ Limited bailout options

On this trail: farmland • river crossing • valley

Route Description

From the jump-off point, I immediately started on a short but steep climb toward the top of the mountain. Locals use this trail regularly, so much of the route is well-trodden.

Early in the ascent, I followed a cemented staircase. Some sections were already missing, but the remaining steps made that part of the climb easier.

As I continued, I passed farmland planted with corn and camote. I also saw cows, goats, and a few carabaos along the route.

The trail passes through several local communities, including settlements deeper in the valley. Other sections felt more isolated because dense vegetation blocked much of the surrounding view.

Later, I descended toward the river that feeds Matun-og Falls. That section gave me the most difficulty because of the steep slope and loose surface.

Trail Conditions

The morning was sunny, and it had not rained for several days. I found the trail very dry, with loose soil that became particularly slippery during the descent toward the river. Based on the condition noted for this route, the same trail can become muddy and slippery after rain.

Shade was limited during the hike, and I did not pass any stores along the route. I encountered locals but few insects. Mobile signal was limited or absent in some sections.

There is also a significant section of river trekking before reaching Matun-og Falls. During this hike, the river section was passable, but this part of the route could become dangerous during heavy rain or a sudden rise in water level.

Additional Notes

Most hikers taking this connection travel in the opposite direction, coming from Matun-og Falls and climbing toward Camp 8. On the steep section I descended, climbing would have been easier than going down on the dry, loose soil.

For the exact route I followed, a trekking pole would have helped with the descent. I carried the expectation of needing at least two liters of water because of the limited shade and the repeated climbs and descents.

]]> Mini Switzerland | Campinsa, Talisay | 2026 GPX https://beesayatv.com/trails/mini-switzerland-campinsa-talisay-2026-gpx/ Wed, 01 Jul 2026 07:41:00 +0000 https://beesayatv.com/?post_type=trail&p=416 Mini Switzerland is a documented 6 km loop hike in Campinsa and Manipis, Talisay City. I followed a route that combined cemented paths, open countryside, hillside trails, and quiet mountain roads before returning to the starting point.

The hike began with a long downhill walk before transitioning into rolling terrain and a steady uphill climb back to the jump-off. Navigation remained straightforward throughout, and I completed this hike in April 2026.

Distance6 km (Loop)
Duration3 - 3.5 hrs

Access

I started in Campinsa, where motorcycle parking was available along the roadside without a parking fee. The jump-off was accessible by concrete road, and private vehicles could reach the area. Public transportation was very limited, although habal-habal services were available.

Why this trail is rated Easy

✓ Easy-to-follow trail
✓ No technical climbing required

On this trail: roads • rolling hills • viewpoint

Route Description

I began by descending a long flight of cemented stairs before joining Manipis Road. From there, the route continued across open hillside trails and rolling terrain leading toward Windy Hills Campsite. Navigation stayed simple throughout, and several sections opened up to views of the surrounding mountains.

After completing the downhill and rolling portions of the loop, I started the steady climb back to Campinsa. Although none of the climbs were technical, the continuous uphill section marked the most demanding part of the return.

Trail Conditions

The weather remained sunny throughout my hike. Most of the route was exposed with very little shade, while the trail stayed dry during my visit. Walking conditions could become muddy after rain. I did not find any stores along the route, and mobile signal remained strong near the jump-off before disappearing farther into the hike. I encountered no other hikers and noticed very few insects.

Additional Notes

Part of the route passed through an active road construction area during my visit in April 2026.
